name: Anuj Kapoor

thesis.text: I go where economics is being rewritten by technology,

strap: Economist, former structurer at Citigroup and EFG, and founder of ventures from Himalayan villages to AI for environmental markets. Board Advisor to the UK All-Party Parliamentary Group on ESG (2023–24). Currently building GreenPeople.earth and Green Intelligence.

tile.title: One question, twenty years
tile.teaser: How economics evolves when new technology arrives.

panel.title: One question, tested in practice for twenty years

blocks.text: How does economics evolve when new technology arrives?

I trained in classical economics, finance and business, then went to the LSE on purpose to study what I believed came next. I spent eight years inside the machinery of capital, structuring cross-asset derivatives at Citigroup and investments at EFG Private Bank.
In 2011–12 Satoshi Nakamoto's paper made that question real: an information system redesigning money, trust and institutions. I left banking in 2012 to follow it.

Since then the pattern has repeated. Find the shift early, learn its economics, technology and incentives deeply, then put it to work in a village, at a market stall, in a carbon registry or inside an AI system.
I'm deep multidisciplinary rather than a generalist. I go far enough into each field to build something that works, then connect it to everything else I know.

panel.title: A classical core, then a technology lens

blocks.text: My MBA gave me the classical core: economics, finance and business. I went to the LSE deliberately to add a second layer, new technology and how economics itself changes with it. In 2024–25 I added a third at Cambridge: sustainability leadership.
